builds.howItPlays: You fill your trash early with Death Mark, a cheap spell that puts the top 3 cards of your deck into your trash and gives you a Shadow Clone, and with Kennen, Storm of Shuriken, a 4-Might unit that trashes 2 more when you play it. Each time you banish a card from your trash, Zed lets you swap a card in your hand for a fresh draw, and once the trash is full Rhasa the Sunderer, a 10-cost unit with 6 Might that costs 1 less for each card in your trash, comes down for almost nothing.
builds.whyYou: You like a deck where the cards you throw away still work for you. You enjoy the running choices this deck asks for each turn: which card to discard with Zed, when to replay Death Mark from your trash, how many cards you need there before Rhasa is cheap enough to play. You still attack from the early turns, so you're never just waiting, but your best turns come from what you set up earlier. If turning a stacked trash into big units for a handful of runes sounds fun, this Zed suits you.
builds.ratingNotes:
Changed 2026-09-25 (re-rate from the deck picks, style "Miracle Zed"). Relabelled Aggro to Midrange, and coordinates moved from 8/8/5/6.5 to 6/7/7/4.5 (pace/stance/complexity/variance), the mean of three scored decks from tools.ts style (labels Midrange, Midrange, Midrange). The old label and numbers came from two launch-era write-ups (riftbound.gg's Vendetta legends guide and riftstorm.gg's launch roundup), which disagreed on pace and complexity and described no current list. Both are dropped from guideUrls, because neither describes this list. deckListUrl was the bare /decks page and is now fabudl's list, the style's first deck. The Build name is the picks' own.
Scored decks:
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/317b1b2d-c46f-4749-9e0a-4fe57808928e ZED - MIRACLE (fabudl; 52 likes, 10191 views) Midrange 6/7/7/4.5
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/414cc8c7-e840-464c-ac97-32d40bd84593 [Zed Tempo] - Unleash the Nashor (pine-exe; guide, matchups) Midrange 6/7/7.5/4.5
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/92f65c8e-e8b3-4e5c-b233-66ade77c3287 Zed - Miracle (VEN) (noxiangrandgeneral; filler, measures the style) Midrange 5.5/6.5/7/4.5
Adjustments (all three sheets): complexity +1 (the Legend's loot has to be re-empowered by banishing, through Flow spells and Shadow Clone attacks, and cashed at the right moment each turn); variance -0.5 (the Legend and Zaun Warrens loot smooth the draws).
Cards that decided each Axis:
- Pace: 8 to 10 units costing 2 or less (Shadow Order Disciple, Traveling Merchant, Tideturner) against 5 to 9 cards costing 5+ (Rhasa the Sunderer, Shadowblade Lurker, Zed, Without a Sound), with Rhasa and Lurker usually cheaper than printed.
- Stance: 20 to 27.5 pressure cards (Noxus Hopeful, Kai'Sa, Survivor, Kennen, Death Mark's Shadow Clone with Assault 4) against only 2 to 3 answers (Star-Crossed). It stays under 7.5 because of the own-plan cards (Seals, Last Rites, Fizz) and the expensive units.
- Complexity: 32 to 33 cards tagged setup or modes: the Burn and Flow trash economy (Death Mark, Perfect Execution, Kennen's Flow grant), Last Rites replaying units from the trash, and Rhasa and Lurker counting the trash.
- Variance: no luck or swing cards, and 60 to 75% of cards run as 3-ofs. Burn fills a trash the deck wants filled, so it isn't counted as luck.
No formula-judgment gap reached 2 on any Axis. The biggest was fabudl's Complexity (formula 6.5, judged 7) and Variance (3.5 against 5).
Legend ability: when you banish a card you own, Zed becomes Empowered. As an Action, disempower and exhaust him to discard 1, then draw 1.

For the reviewer: the picks folded Battleaxe Movement Zed, an Aggro style (6.5/7.5/7/5.5), into this Midrange Build instead of making it a second Build. It sits within 0.5 of Miracle on every Axis, so it fails Distinct. Endless Riches pulls away only on Variance (about 6.5). guideUrls are the three scored deck pages. pine-exe's page carries the author's guide and matchups.
